$comment: The inquiry definition of governance/motivation.schema.yaml as of Blueprint Schema 2.8.103, before an inquiry could name its addressee. inquiry-addressee.test.mjs puts it back in place of the current one.

inquiry.description: Governance inquiry - an unresolved strategic or stakeholder concern that needs investigation or decision before work can proceed. Distinct from QN### (domain competency questions that model the reason for a domain to exist). Inquiries are temporary governance artifacts; questions are permanent domain knowledge requirements.

category.description: Inquiry domain classification. business=revenue/market impact, technical=architecture/infrastructure, ux=user experience, legal=regulatory/compliance, data=data quality/availability, dependency=external blocking factor, feasibility=can we do this, strategic=direction/vision, organizational=team/process.

question_refs.description: Domain competency questions (QN###) that prompted this governance inquiry.

finding_refs.title: Findings
finding_refs.description: Quality findings (FN###) this inquiry is about or was prompted by. The inquiry owns the link and a finding carries no reference back, so an inquiry that closes leaves nothing stale on the finding; the inquiries open on a finding are read in the reverse direction. An id no quality file declares is a cross-reference error.

stakeholders.description: Actors who care about the resolution.

affects.description: Blueprint entities this inquiry touches: where it sticks on the domain model, so a story board or a wall can pin it beside the operation, concept, bounded context, service, package, capability, story or process activity it is about.

context_refs.description: Bounded contexts / slices affected, by scope name. A name, not a reference: it builds no edge. Name a bounded context by its arch id in `bounded_context_refs`.

bounded_context_refs.title: Bounded contexts
bounded_context_refs.description: Bounded contexts (BC###) affected as a whole, by arch id. A typed reference: an id no arch file declares is a cross-reference error. A scope name belongs in `context_refs`.

service_refs.title: Services
service_refs.description: Architecture services (SVC###) affected as a whole, by arch id. A typed reference: an id no arch file declares is a cross-reference error.

package_refs.title: Packages
package_refs.description: Third-party packages (PKG###) affected as a whole, by the id their `packages:` declaration carries. A typed reference: an id no arch file declares is a cross-reference error.

process_refs.description: Business processes affected, for a concern about a flow as a whole rather than one of its operations.

process_activity_refs.title: Process activities
process_activity_refs.description: Process activities (PA###) this inquiry is about, for an open question about one step of a flow: who does it, what it takes or produces, whether it happens at all. Each is the exact id its process declares, so it names one activity only where no other process declares the same id. An id no process declares is a cross-reference error.

capability_refs.title: Capabilities
capability_refs.description: Capabilities and features (CAP###) this inquiry bears on, each named by its declared id. A typed reference: an id no capability file declares is a cross-reference error. The inquiry belongs to each capability named here and to no other: a named capability's children, its parent and the capabilities that share an operation with it are not implied, so name every capability or feature the inquiry is about.

owner.description: A person or role (ACT###) or a team (TM###) who drives this inquiry to its resolution. Distinct from owned_by (the unit accountable for it).

blocking.description: True if this inquiry blocks downstream work.

resolution.description: Answer or decision once the inquiry is resolved.

resolved.description: DEPRECATED - derived from `status`, which is the single source of the lifecycle. `resolved` is true exactly when `status` is `resolved` or `closed`. Still accepted so existing documents keep loading; a consumer should read `status`.

status.description: Inquiry lifecycle: open=logged, investigating=actively being researched, resolved=answer found, closed=resolution accepted, deferred=postponed.
